method.mos: UTMOS22-strong (SpeechMOS); biased against high pitch - compare within a voice only
method.rtf: seconds of compute per second of audio (lower is faster), per sentence item, model already loaded and warmed up

spoken.hyp: Before any training run, we froze the evaluation set and put it somewhere the training code could not reach. That separation matters more than any single hyperparameter. The first used supervised fine-tuning, where the model imitates annotated answers one token at a time. A held-out set is a promise: these examples will tell us the truth, because the model has never seen them. We then trained two systems. The second used direct preference optimisation, where the model sees a better and a worse answer to the same prompt and is nudged toward the better one. On the tool-policy metrics, both looked like progress. The over-call rate fell, the F one score rose, and the curves were smooth. It was only when we asked ordinary questions, the kind with no tool involved at all, that the picture changed. The model had started to refuse. Not occasionally, and not at random, but systematically, as if refusal were a place it kept falling back into.

spoken.hyp: Before any training run, we froze the evaluation set and put it somewhere the training code could not reach. That separation matters more than any single hyperparameter. A held-out set is a promise. These examples will tell us the truth, because the model has never seen them. We then trained two systems. The first used supervised fine-tuning, where the model imitates annotated answers one token at a time. The second used direct preference optimization, where the model sees a better and a worse answer to the same prompt and is nudged toward the better one. On the tool policy metrics, both looked like progress. The over-call rate fell, the F1 score rose and the curves were smooth. It was only when we asked ordinary questions, the kind with no tool involved at all, that the picture changed. The model had started to refuse. Not occasionally, and not at random, but systematically, as if refusal were a place it kept falling back into.
